title: SRE Weekly Ops Sync — prep + reliability review (draft)
content:
Meeting: SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review (prep notes)
Owner: Jordan Lee (oncall coordinator)
Date for sync: 2026-03-04 weekly 09:30 PT
Attendees (expected): Priya, Miguel, Samira, Evan, oncall-rotations

Agenda (30m)
- Quick updates (5m) — oncall highlight, capacity changes
- SLO review (8m) — availability, latency, error budget burn
- Paging trends & noise (5m) — sources of spike, paging rules tuning
- Top incidents / RCA updates (7m) — INC-2026-031, INC-2026-033 status
- Action items & owners (5m)

Prep notes / bullets to surface
1) SLO summary (month-to-date, Mar 1–Mar 4)
   - Hosted API availability SLO target: 99.9%
     - MTD achieved: 99.92% (within SLO)
     - Recent blip: 2026-03-02 14:42–15:06 UTC region-eu-west1 — brief routing config flapping contributed (~0.03% hit)
   - Inference endpoint latency (text-gen) P95 target: 200ms
     - MTD observed: P95 = 240ms (target miss)
     - Root cause hypothesis: increased batch sizes from a new client rollout + backend GC pauses
     - Error budget burn: 36% MTD for latency SLO
   - Embeddings throughput SLO: on track (98.7% of target)

2) Paging trends (last 7 days)
   - Total pages: 112 (up from 97 previous week, +15%)
   - Most common page reasons: high tail latency (45%), host OOMs (20%), downstream auth failures (15%)
   - Top noisy alert: "inference-host-cpu-threshold" firing during scheduled compaction windows — false positives when compaction runs coincide with small traffic bursts
   - Action: propose suppressing that alert during scheduled compaction windows for non-prod pools (see action items)

3) Top incidents (brief)
   - INC-2026-031: inference-host-22 OOM on 2026-03-01 03:18 UTC
     - Impact: degraded capacity for ~12m, some requests retried to other pools
     - Cause: memory growth in batching path after recent serving-runtime PR that changes batch aggregation logic (PR #1423)
     - Current status: mitigation deployed (limit batch size to 8 on affected pool); full fix in progress
     - Linked: JIRA INC-2026-031, GH PR 1423
   - INC-2026-033: auth service 401 spikes (2026-03-02 14:40–15:10 UTC)
     - Impact: increased client errors, small % of calls failed fast
     - Cause: intermittent token refresh failures in eu-west1 due to upstream rate limit change
     - Current status: contacted partner team, temporary retry/backoff added in gateway, long-term fix scheduled

4) Known risks to call out
   - New client rollout that increases default batch windows — if rollout continues we may see sustained latency SLO burn
   - Memory leak risk in the batch aggregation codepath (INC-2026-031) until full root cause is fixed
   - Scaling policy for dedicated pools: autoscaler cooldown is conservative, can lead to capacity shortage during bursty traffic

5) Proposed items for discussion / decisions needed
   - Approve temporary alert suppression during compaction windows for non-prod pools (owners: Samira + Miguel)
   - Approve rolling throttle on new client rollout to limit default batch size to 8 until fix shipped (owner: Priya)
   - Prioritize full RCA / memory retention fix for batch aggregation in next sprint (owner: serving-runtime team, tracked in GH/PR and Jira)

Action items (tracked individually below)
- AI-1: Samira to add suppression rule for "inference-host-cpu-threshold" during scheduled compaction windows for non-prod pools. Due: 2026-03-06. (linked: INC-2026-031)
- AI-2: Priya to request client-team to rollback/limit new batch defaults to 8 and monitor latency for 48h. Due: 2026-03-05. (linked: slack thread #client-rollout)
- AI-3: Miguel to instrument heap retention metrics on batch aggregator and attach flamegraphs to INC-2026-031. Due: 2026-03-07. (linked: GH PR 1423)
- AI-4: Jordan to update oncall runbook with mitigation steps for OOMs and add checklist for emergency batch-size throttling. Due: 2026-03-05.
- AI-5: Evan to adjust autoscaler cooldown on dedicated pools for bursty traffic experiments and report effect. Due: 2026-03-10.

Notes / evidence to bring to the sync
- Grafana: SLO overview + latency heatmap (see linked artifacts)
- Flamegraphs from affected host (Miguel will upload)
- Client rollout release notes + PRs (Priya to summarize)

Open questions / discussion points
- Do we want to temporarily tighten the latency SLO definition for new beta customers? Pros/cons? (bring up in meeting)
- Are current paging thresholds tuned for new hardware (A800 vs A100) differences? Might need pool-specific thresholds.

Attachments / links to include in meeting notes
- Grafana SLO dashboard (linked)
- JIRA: INC-2026-031, INC-2026-033 (linked)
- GH PR: serving-runtime PR #1423 (linked)

Draft messaging for execs (if asked)
- Short: We had two short incidents last week; availability SLO held but latency SLO is burning faster than expected due to increased batch sizes from a client rollout and a memory-growth regression. Short-term mitigations deployed; full fix prioritized for next sprint. Will update after RCA and client throttling.

Next steps before sync
- All owners to confirm status in ticket comments before meeting
- Samira/Miguel to prepare alert suppression proposal snippet for immediate review

-- end of prep notes (draft)

Priya - request client-team limit batch default to 8 and monitor (due 2026-03-05)
Miguel - instrument heap retention and attach flamegraphs to INC-2026-031 (due 2026-03-07)
Jordan - update oncall runbook with OOM mitigation + checklist (due 2026-03-05)
